classification.reason: China supplies the large majority of Pakistan's major arms imports (SIPRI estimates 63-80% depending on period) and has invested heavily in Pakistan through CPEC. For China, Pakistan offers a reliable land route to the Arabian Sea (Gwadar) and a strategic counterweight tying down India's military attention on two fronts.
classification.source: SIPRI Trends in International Arms Transfers 2024

strategic_issues: CPEC investments face periodic security threats from militant groups inside Pakistan
Pakistan's debt exposure to Chinese loans has become a recurring point of economic strain
trade_dependencies: Pakistan is heavily dependent on Chinese loans and infrastructure financing (CPEC)

energy_relationship.notes: Limited direct energy trade; cooperation is centered on infrastructure and arms rather than energy

military_relationship.posture: very close, described by both sides as an all-weather partnership
military_relationship.notes: China supplies the majority of Pakistan's fighter aircraft, air-defence systems, and naval vessels; joint military exercises are frequent

diplomatic_relationship.posture: closely aligned, described by both governments as 'higher than the mountains, deeper than the seas'
diplomatic_relationship.notes: China has historically shielded Pakistan diplomatically at the UN Security Council on Kashmir-related and terrorism-designation issues

escalation_factors: Continued Chinese arms resupply to Pakistan directly affects the India-Pakistan military balance

_meta.data_quality: sourced for arms-trade share, demo for other figures
_meta.source: SIPRI Trends in International Arms Transfers 2024
